A pure-white fawn steps onto a mossy ledge above the stream, completely unafraid.
A slow fall of cherry-blossom petals drifts down through the gorge, catching the warm afternoon light.
A soft swirl of glowing pixies rises alongside the waterfall like living, breathing light.
A flight of white swans glides silently along the stream, trailing small silver ripples behind them.
A pure-white unicorn stands at the water's edge, its mane lifting gently in the mist.
A great low moon hangs soft and full above the canyon rim, pale gold and tender.
A procession of fae-lights moves slowly along the rope bridge, each one warm as a candle.
A white owl glides without a sound along the gorge wall, wings spread wide and still.
A little rope-pulled boat crosses the stream, its single lantern throwing honey-gold light on the water.
A red fox pauses on the wet rocks, watching the lantern boat pass with quiet curiosity.
Glow-moths rise in a soft, slow cloud from the tall reeds near the village bank.
A rainbow appears in the waterfall mist, faint and trembling, arching over the mossy stones below.
A young otter sits upright on a flat rock, holding something small and bright in its paws.
Three white swans rest on the calm water beneath the bridge, perfectly still in the blue dusk.
The white fawn lowers its head to drink, its reflection shimmering gently in the shallow stream.
Fae-lights drift free of the rope bridge and float upward slowly into the soft evening sky.
The glowing pixies spiral higher up the waterfall, their light turning the falling water pale rose.
A handful of cherry-blossom petals settles on the lantern boat's bow, delicate as a held breath.
The white unicorn turns and walks slowly back into the silver birch trees at the gorge's edge.
Glow-moths settle briefly on the rope bridge ropes, making the whole bridge shimmer like a strand of stars.
The low moon's reflection stretches long and golden across the still water below the canyon rim.
The white owl lands silently on a mossy post at the village dock, blinking once, slowly.
A soft bloom of fae-light rises from the reeds and drifts across the stream like a sigh.
The otter slips back into the water without a splash, leaving only one small, widening ring.
The last cherry-blossom petal turns in the air above the gorge, catches the light, and is gone.
